claims.text: The candidate initial state is a random, single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy such as W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf or HfNbTaTiZr.
Cr-Hf pairs exhibit strong attraction and strongly negative SRO parameters in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf.
Cr-V has a negative enthalpy of mixing and a strong segregation tendency in W-Ta-Cr-V.
Strong attractive interactions such as Cr-Hf or Cr-V drive SRO clusters to form a percolating network.
A suitable potential-energy surface must explicitly capture the strong pair attractions that stabilize the proposed SRO clusters.
Cr-Hf chemical order is present over at least part of the proposed 300–1000 K interval and vanishes near 1080 K for the cited W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf composition.
Within the proposed annealing interval, macroscopic phase separation is kinetically inhibited and distinct precipitates do not form.
Isothermal annealing causes SRO clusters to grow and cross a percolation threshold without producing a second phase.
The relevant regime has an SRO correlation length greater than the phonon mean free path but remains below the threshold for macroscopic phase separation.
Percolating chemically ordered clusters create a continuous, low-disorder pathway for phonon transport.
Standard point-defect scattering and serial/parallel mixing models predict a monotonic reduction in thermal conductivity as SRO magnitude increases.
A connected ordered sublattice reduces mass-fluctuation scattering along the SRO-cluster network.
Phonons propagate with less resistance through the percolating SRO network than through a purely random solid solution.
Reduced resistance along the ordered network counteracts scattering in the remaining disordered matrix.
Thermal conductivity undergoes a sharp nonlinear increase, or a substantially smaller decrease than conventional models predict, near the SRO percolation threshold.
The proposed enhancement fails below the percolation threshold, where SRO clusters remain isolated.
A potential that underestimates the relevant pair attraction will instead produce random mixing and eliminate the proposed effect.
The cited evidence does not quantify the thermal-conductivity effect of percolating SRO in single-phase bcc refractory alloys.
The proposed test varies Cr-Hf ratio and annealing history, determines SRO morphology and percolation by simulation and APT, and measures thermal conductivity by TDTR.

The hypothesis is falsified if conductivity follows a monotonic scattering-model trend without a nonlinear anomaly near percolation, with conductivity at the threshold below that of the random solid solution.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits a smaller-than-modeled conductivity decrease, which could still leave conductivity below the random-solid-solution value, but the falsification rule declares any below-random value at the threshold to invalidate the mechanism.
